state-college-pa.name: State College
state-college-pa.note: Drive times are rough. Parks can close day-use areas at dusk, so check hours before you go.

spots.caution: State College's lights sit right below, so faint stars and faint aurora get washed out.
spots.name: Jo Hays Vista
spots.why: Roadside overlook on PA-26 at the top of Tussey Mountain, with a wide open view north and west over the valley. The closest place with a clear northern horizon.

spots.caution: Check park hours for after-dark access.
spots.name: Black Moshannon State Park
spots.why: Up on the plateau northwest of town and well away from its glow. The lake gives you an open sky and a reflection.

spots.caution: Check park hours for after-dark access.
spots.name: Bald Eagle State Park
spots.why: A long lake with wide horizons in several directions. Good when you want the Moon or the sunset over water.

spots.caution: Ridges on both sides cut off the low horizon, so it is poor for aurora.
spots.name: Greenwood Furnace State Park
spots.why: A sheltered valley south of the ridges with very little light around it.

spots.caution: White light is restricted on the field. Bring a red flashlight and arrive before dark.
spots.name: Cherry Springs State Park
spots.why: A certified International Dark Sky Park in Potter County with a public night-sky viewing area. Worth the trip for a big shower peak or a strong aurora forecast.
